stimuli.title: Seven people live on different floors of a seven-storey building. Floor 1 is the bottom floor, and floor 7 is the top floor.
stimuli.body:
Clues:
1. Priya is at floor 7.
2. Anika is exactly 3 positions above Zoya.
3. Kavya is exactly 2 positions above Anika.
4. Bhavna is immediately above Isha.
stimuli.solution: floor 1: Zoya; floor 2: Isha; floor 3: Bhavna; floor 4: Anika; floor 5: Meera; floor 6: Kavya; floor 7: Priya

stimuli.title: Seven labelled boxes are stacked vertically, with one box in each position.
stimuli.body:
Clues:
1. Lakshya is exactly 2 positions above Deepa.
2. Kriti is exactly 3 positions above Yash.
3. Esha is at position 4 from the bottom.
4. In the stated ordering, Zoya comes before Farhan, and Farhan comes before Esha.
stimuli.solution: position 1 from the bottom: Zoya; position 2 from the bottom: Farhan; position 3 from the bottom: Yash; position 4 from the bottom: Esha; position 5 from the bottom: Deepa; position 6 from the bottom: Kriti; position 7 from the bottom: Lakshya

stimuli.title: Seven people have interviews in seven consecutive months from January to July, one per month.
stimuli.body:
Clues:
1. Bharat is at January.
2. Chitra is exactly 3 positions later than Tarun.
3. Ravi is exactly 2 positions later than Esha.
4. Tarun is exactly 2 positions later than Jai.
stimuli.solution: January: Bharat; February: Jai; March: Esha; April: Tarun; May: Ravi; June: Harish; July: Chitra

stimuli.title: Seven employees hold seven distinct ranks (rank 1 is junior-most and rank 7 is senior-most).
stimuli.body:
Clues:
1. Deepa is exactly 2 positions senior to Bharat.
2. Lakshya is exactly 3 positions senior to Deepa.

stimuli.solution: rank 1: Uday; rank 2: Bharat; rank 3: Charu; rank 4: Deepa; rank 5: Pooja; rank 6: Farhan; rank 7: Lakshya

stimuli.title: In a certain coded language, each word has one unique code.
stimuli.body:
river yellow velvet = li qa fi
river golden saffron = mu fi ve
velvet timber saffron = ve te li
golden yellow timber = mu qa te
stimuli.solution: river=fi, velvet=li, yellow=qa, saffron=ve, golden=mu, timber=te

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain U < V ≤ R ≤ W = Q, decide which conclusions follow. I: W = Q. II: U > V.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is always true and II is not necessarily true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain T ≥ V < X < Q < R, decide which conclusions follow. I: T < Q. II: Q ≤ R.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is not necessarily true and II is always true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain Z ≤ P < S < V > W, decide which conclusions follow. I: P ≤ W. II: S < V.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain Q ≥ S > P > T < U, decide which conclusions follow. I: T = U. II: P < T.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain Z > U < R < Q > T, decide which conclusions follow. I: R < Q. II: Z = Q.

questions.stem: Statements: Some bakers are poets. Some poets are singers. Conclusions: I. Some bakers are singers. II. Some poets are bakers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The two Some overlaps need not coincide; Some A are B converts to Some B are A.

questions.stem: Statements: All coders are farmers. Some drivers are coders. Conclusions: I. Some drivers are farmers. II. Some farmers are drivers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The existing C∩A members must lie in B, proving both conclusions.

questions.stem: Statements: No bakers are coders. All poets are coders. Some poets are coders. Conclusions: I. No bakers are poets. II. Some poets are not bakers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: All C members belong to B, disjoint from A; some C are explicitly given.

questions.stem: Statements: Some workers are teachers. Some teachers are dancers. Conclusions: I. Some workers are dancers. II. All dancers are workers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The specified intersections do not force A and C to overlap or include one another.

questions.stem: Statements: Some runners are drivers. All drivers are workers. Conclusions: I. Some runners are workers. II. All runners are workers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Some A–B members must be C; not all A need be C.

questions.stem: Ritu walks 25 km north, then 20 km east, then 5 km south and finally 5 km west. What is her shortest distance from the starting point?

questions.stem: A cyclist travels 45 km north, 20 km east, 25 km south and 5 km west. What total distance did the cyclist travel?

questions.stem: Compare x and y. Equation I: x² + 7x + 0 = 0. Equation II: y² + 7y + 10 = 0. Which option is always correct?
questions.explanation: Roots of x are -7 and 0; roots of y are -5 and -2. Hence Relationship cannot be established.

questions.stem: Compare x and y. Equation I: x² + 1x + 0 = 0. Equation II: y² + 11y + 30 = 0. Which option is always correct?
questions.explanation: Roots of x are -1 and 0; roots of y are -6 and -5. Hence x > y.

questions.stem: Compare x and y. Equation I: x² + 3x + 0 = 0. Equation II: y² + 8y + 15 = 0. Which option is always correct?
questions.explanation: Roots of x are -3 and 0; roots of y are -5 and -3. Hence x ≥ y.

questions.stem: Compare x and y. Equation I: x² + 13x + 42 = 0. Equation II: y² + 5y + 6 = 0. Which option is always correct?
questions.explanation: Roots of x are -7 and -6; roots of y are -3 and -2. Hence x < y.

questions.stem: Compare x and y. Equation I: x² + 8x + 15 = 0. Equation II: y² + 3y + 0 = 0. Which option is always correct?
questions.explanation: Roots of x are -5 and -3; roots of y are -3 and 0. Hence x ≤ y.
